guide.summary: A planning guide for the integration conversation. The final API and environment contract is agreed separately.

sections.heading: 1. Define the operating scope
sections.body: List countries, direction of funds, counterparties, currencies and responsibility for each stage.

sections.heading: 2. Agree data and references
sections.body: Identify required fields, identifiers, validation rules and the reference shared across systems.

sections.heading: 3. Agree events and recovery
sections.body: Define authoritative statuses, acknowledgement, duplicate handling, retries and manual escalation.

sections.heading: 4. Agree reporting
sections.body: Map gross, fees, FX, net values, timestamps and reconciliation responsibilities where applicable.

sections.heading: 5. Test and launch
sections.body: Agree positive, exception, duplicate and recovery scenarios with the actual integration contract.

lifecycle.h1: Keep the instruction connected to the outcome.
lifecycle.summary: A conceptual model for discussing instructions, processing, confirmation and exceptions.

sections.heading: Instruction
sections.body: An instruction being received is distinct from a payment being completed.

sections.heading: Processing
sections.body: A pending state records work in progress. Its expected transitions and escalation rules must be agreed.

sections.heading: Confirmation
sections.body: Define the authoritative event and record that your operation uses to recognise the outcome.

sections.heading: Exceptions
sections.body: Agree rejection, failure, reversal and unresolved states where they apply. Do not collapse them into one visual success state.

webhooks.h1: Make a change of state explicit.
webhooks.summary: Plan event delivery and recovery using the actual event contract agreed for your integration.

sections.heading: Identity and authenticity
sections.body: Agree event IDs, signing or authentication, secret rotation and accepted verification rules.

sections.heading: Duplicates and ordering
sections.body: Design consumers to recognise repeated events and tolerate the documented ordering behaviour.

sections.heading: Acknowledgement and retry
sections.body: Agree response codes, timeout boundaries, retry policy and operational ownership.

sections.heading: Recovery and observability
sections.body: Record safe correlation IDs and provide a route to investigate missing or unresolved events.

ownerGates: Replace planning guidance with versioned signed integration details before labelling API documentation

sections.heading: Agree the close
